recognize_zh: 低倍下淋巴結內有一束束呈流線狀排列的紡錘形細胞（spindle cell），穿插在淋巴組織之間並繞過濾泡，與正常結構容易混淆；需靠 Melan-A、S100 等免疫染色確認為轉移性紡錘細胞黑色素瘤。
features: Sweeping fascicles of spindle cells with elongated, hyperchromatic nuclei and eosinophilic cytoplasm
Spindle cells track through sinuses and interfollicular zones around lymphoid aggregates
Preserved dense small-lymphocyte areas (follicle-like) at the right
Occasional mitotic figures within the spindle cell bands
No melanin pigment visible at this low magnification
describe_en: Section of lymph node at low power shows fascicles of spindle cells that sweep through the sinuses and interfollicular areas, dividing the residual lymphoid tissue into nodules while sparing follicles. The spindle cells have elongated hyperchromatic nuclei and eosinophilic cytoplasm, with occasional mitoses; melanin pigment is not evident. At this magnification the infiltrate can mimic nodal stroma or capsular trabeculae. With the reported Melan-A and S100 positivity, findings are consistent with metastatic spindle cell melanoma.

ddx.vs: Kaposi sarcoma forms slit-like vascular spaces with extravasated red cells and hyaline globules and is HHV8 (LANA-1) positive, not S100/Melan-A positive.
IDCS is S100 positive but negative for Melan-A, HMB45 and SOX10-associated melanocytic markers and lacks a primary skin melanoma history.
FDCS shows whorled spindle cells expressing CD21, CD23 and CD35, and is negative for S100 and Melan-A.
These are distinguished immunohistochemically by cytokeratin or lineage-specific markers (e.g. desmin, SMA) with negative melanocytic markers.
